stem: Quit India movement began on:
expl: The historic session of the All India Congress Committee began on the 7th August, 1942 A.D. and concluded on 8th August, 1942 A.D. at Gowalia Tank Maidan (now August Kranti Ground), Bombay. Quit India movement began on 9th August, 1942 A.D. The Committee asserted India’s right to freedom and decided to start a mass struggle with non-violent means on the widest possible scale. Addressing the conference, Gandhiji gave the call “Do or Die,” either to get India free or to die in this attempt. But before the Movement could be launched Gandhiji and all other leaders of the Congress were imprisoned under Operation Zero Hour. Gandhiji and Sarojini Naidu were kept in Aga Khan Palace at Poona (now Pune). The Movement of 1942 A.D. mostly affected the State of Bombay, Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, United Province (U.P.) and Madras. Though the whole country participated in this Movement.

stem: With the news of Gandhi and other Congress leaders arrest in 1942, a riot in Bihar took place, leading to a total breakdown in the rail services. The most affected area was :
expl: On August 9, 1942 Gandhiji and other main leaders of Congress were arrested. Police launched a suppression cycle to crack down on the Movement. Outraged by the suppression of the police, the public attacked at several places. Police stations, Railway stations and post offi ces were on their targets. Rail lines were uprooted at several places . As a result, rail services were disrupted completely. Medinipur district of Bengal, Baliya district of Uttar Pradesh and Munger district of Bihar were the centers of public anger. The incident of uprooting railway tracks had mostly happened in Bihar. Munger was the most affected district which remained cut off from the outside world for 2 weeks.

stem: After Quit India Movement, C. Rajagopalachari issued a pamphlet entitled “The Way Out.” Which one of the following was a proposal in this pamphlet?

options.label: a
options.text: The establishment of a “War Advisory Council” composed of representatives of British India and the Indian States

options.label: b
options.text: Reconstitution of the Central Executive Council in such a way that all its members, except the Governor-General and the Commander-in-Chief, should be Indian leaders

options.label: c
options.text: Fresh elections to the Central and Provincial Legislatures to be held at the end of 1945 and the Constitution-making body to be convened as soon as possible

options.label: d
options.text: A solution to the Constitutional deadlock

expl: C. Rajagopalachari’s formula was a proposal formulated by Chakravarthi Rajagopalachari to solve the political deadlock between INC and All India Muslim League regarding Independence of India from the British. Rajagopalachari devised a proposal in 1944 A.D. called ‘The way out’ for Congress to offer the league the Muslim Pakistan based on plebiscite (the direct vote of all the members of an electorate on an important public question such as a change in the Constitution). The formula was opposed even by Congress. Jinnah also rejected the proposal and the talks failed.

stem: 'Operation Rubicon' was the code word proposed to be adopted by British Government in India with reference to which of the following?

options.label: a
options.text: Gandhi's fast unto death in Jail

options.label: c
options.text: Gandhi's participation in Round Table Conference

expl: During Quit India movement while imprisoned in the Aga Khan Palace, Mahatma Gandhi's health was rapidly declining due to his fast unto death. 'Operation Rubicon' was secret code word to be adopted by the British Government in India, if Gandhiji died..
